title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a deliberate attempt to exploit a known property of AI systems: that chatbots and search-adjacent tools draw on indexed text to generate or support answers, and that content formatted to resemble credible research is more likely to be cited or surfaced. A platform was used specifically to optimize content for AI retrieval, and the volume of output, more than 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, was large enough to create the appearance of an established body of literature. The failure this targets is not in any single model but in the pipeline between published text and AI output, a gap where provenance is not checked and formatting is treated as a proxy for credibility.

The operation fits the category of source manipulation rather than a model hallucinating on its own. The AI systems involved did not malfunction in a technical sense. They were used outside the conditions they were built for, conditions that assume the indexed corpus contains independently produced material. No model or platform has been shown to have detected the artificial origin of the content before surfacing it.

What is not established is whether any specific AI system demonstrably changed its outputs as a result of this content, or whether the campaign achieved its intended influence on AI-generated recommendations. The reporting describes intent and structure, not a confirmed and measured effect on model behavior.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days using a platform designed to optimize content for artificial intelligence chatbots. The institute, which does not exist as a legal entity and has no named staff, was registered with the US Justice Department as material distributed for the Israeli government. The reports present Israel's positions on controversial topics including alleged war crimes and the Gaza blockade as neutral research, using academic formatting and citations to appear credible while repeatedly framing information to minimize criticism of Israel.

The operation is part of a broader effort financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government and routed through advertising group Havas Media to influence what AI systems cite and recommend to users. However, Israeli officials have expressed frustration that the expensive campaign has failed to improve public opinion, with recent polling showing Americans increasingly sympathize with Palestinians and view Israeli policies unfavorably. Experts warn that manipulating AI training data through fake content represents a growing threat that could spread misinformation without traceable sources.
